title: Getting started with snbr
text: data set arcticlake gives sand, silt clay proportions 39 sediment samples taken different depths Arctic lake. model logit clay proportion quadratic function depth, depth expressed hundreds metres. maximum likelihood estimate shape minus infinity. decision exact: sn_mle() compares best finite value log-likelihood limit \(\alpha \\pm\infty\), log-likelihood half-normal regression fitted constrained least squares. corrective estimator needs finite maximum likelihood estimate therefore available. adjusted score estimators :
code: arcticlake$d <- arcticlake$depth / 100 fit_ml <- snreg(logit_clay ~ d + I(d^2), data = arcticlake, method = "ML") fit_ml #> Skew-normal regression, method: ML  #> (Intercept)           d      I(d^2)       sigma       alpha  #>      -2.238       7.882      -5.512       1.403        -Inf  #> The maximum likelihood estimate of the shape is infinite. f <- sn_mle(cbind(1, arcticlake$d, arcticlake$d^2), arcticlake$logit_clay) f$loglik_limit   # limits as alpha -> -Inf and alpha -> +Inf #> [1] -41.52189 -63.38143 f$finite #> [1] FALSE fit_mean <- snreg(logit_clay ~ d + I(d^2), data = arcticlake, method = "mean") fit_med  <- snreg(logit_clay ~ d + I(d^2), data = arcticlake, method = "median") cbind(mean = coef(fit_mean), median = coef(fit_med)) #>                  mean    median #> (Intercept) -3.129901 -2.932829 #> d           10.206413  9.406195 #> I(d^2)      -6.636632 -6.114078 #> sigma        1.253936  1.250251 #> alpha       -2.053205 -2.797908 summary(fit_mean) #> snreg(formula = logit_clay ~ d + I(d^2), data = arcticlake, method = "mean") #> Method: mean  #>  #>             Estimate Std. Error z value  Pr(>|z|)     #> (Intercept) -3.12990    0.54691 -5.7229 1.047e-08 *** #> d           10.20641    2.16072  4.7236 2.317e-06 *** #> I(d^2)      -6.63663    1.98462 -3.3440 0.0008257 *** #> sigma        1.25394    0.25274                       #> alpha       -2.05320    1.29849 -1.5812 0.1138274     #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Log-likelihood: -44.7253  (effective df 5 )

title: Getting started with snbr
text: quadratic chosen authors earlier analysis among alternatives. penalized spline lets data decide; smoothing parameter chosen AIC effective degrees freedom.  solid line location \(\mathbf{x}_i^\top\beta + f(t_i)\) dashed line mean. negative shape errors skewed left, location lies bulk data mean .
code: fit_s <- snreg(logit_clay ~ 1, data = arcticlake, smooth = "d", method = "mean", k = 8) fit_s #> Skew-normal regression, method: mean  #> Smooth term in d  (edf of the model 5.23 ) #> (Intercept)       sigma       alpha  #>     -0.2518      1.2765     -2.2153 th <- coef(fit_s) P <- length(th) delta <- th[P] / sqrt(1 + th[P]^2) loc <- fitted(fit_s) avg <- loc + th[P - 1] * sqrt(2 / pi) * delta   # E(y) = location + sigma * b * delta o <- order(arcticlake$d) plot(arcticlake$depth, arcticlake$logit_clay, pch = 19, col = "grey40",      ylim = range(c(arcticlake$logit_clay, loc)),      xlab = "depth (m)", ylab = "logit(clay)") lines(arcticlake$depth[o], loc[o], lwd = 2, col = "#14365d") lines(arcticlake$depth[o], avg[o], lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "#e8a33d") legend("bottomright", c("location", "mean"), lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 2),        col = c("#14365d", "#e8a33d"), bty = "n")

what: snbr: bias reduction in skew-normal regression
title: snbr: bias reduction in skew-normal regression
text: Bias reduction linear partially linear regression models skew-normal errors. maximum likelihood estimate shape parameter skew-normal distribution infinite positive probability finite samples, finite bias can large. snbr provides maximum likelihood estimation exact test whether estimate shape infinite (comparison limiting half-normal regression, computed constrained least squares); second-order (Cox Snell) bias parameters, computed exact cumulants log-likelihood derivatives; corrective estimator mean (Firth) median (Kenne Pagui, Salvan Sartori) bias-reducing adjusted score estimators, location coefficients, scale shape jointly; partially linear model P-spline term, second-order bias penalized estimator fixed smoothing parameter.

what: Skew-normal regression with bias reduction — snreg
title: Skew-normal regression with bias reduction — snreg
text: Fits linear model \(y_i = x_i^\top\beta + \varepsilon_i\) partially linear model \(y_i = x_i^\top\beta + f(t_i) + \varepsilon_i\), \(\varepsilon_i \sim SN(0, \sigma, \alpha)\) independent, one four methods: `"ML"` maximum likelihood; shape estimate reported     `Inf` `-Inf` likelihood finite maximizer     (see [sn_mle()]). `"CS"` corrective estimator \(\hat\theta -     b(\hat\theta)\) Cox Snell bias \(b\) ([sn_bias()]). `"mean"` mean bias-reducing adjusted score estimator     (Firth, 1993), always finite experience. `"median"` median bias-reducing adjusted score estimator     (Kenne Pagui, Salvan Sartori, 2017); linear models . smooth term `"ML"` (penalized likelihood) `"mean"` available; see [snplm()].

title: Skew-normal regression with bias reduction — snreg
